title: Registry and archive downloads refuse URLs that are not credential-free HTTPS
summary: `fetchBounded` (`@inventarch/distribution/internal/bounded-fetch`), the one request behind registry documents and remote archives, now checks the URL itself before any request, even when its caller did not. It requests a URL only in the shape `new URL` gives a credential-free HTTPS URL without query or fragment: `https://`, a lowercase host or a bracketed IPv6 address, an optional port, and a path that starts with `/` and uses only ASCII letters, digits, `%` and `!$&'()*+,-./:;=@[]^_|~`. Any other URL, such as one with credentials, a query, a fragment, another scheme, an uppercase or non-ASCII host, or a space, refuses with `IA-DIST-INPUT-INVALID` and names the URL. Every URL that `parseRegistryBase` and the archive check admit still passes, including an archive URL that ends in a bare `?` or `#`, so registry, catalog and restore reads behave as before; a hand-built `RegistryBase`, or a direct `fetchBounded` call, with a URL outside that shape now refuses. Redirects, the 30-second timeout and the byte bounds are unchanged.
